stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key ML/NLP tags such as 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's Llama models.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and features native support for DFlash and image input via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: Sam Altman says OpenAI won’t go public until its models are safe
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has stated that the company will not pursue an Initial Public Offering (IPO) in the near future.
The primary prerequisite for going public is OpenAI's ability to provide stronger assurances regarding the safety of its AI models.
Altman indicated a commitment to continued AI progress while prioritizing safety improvements over immediate financial milestones.

stories.title: OpenAI launches Dots, its Muse competitor
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: OpenAI is launching 'Dots,' a new line of always-on, agentic AI assistants.
Dots is positioned as a direct competitor to Meta's Muse AI.
The assistants will operate in the background across connected apps, learning user preferences, and are powered by GPT-6 Astra.

stories.title: AMD acquires World Labs AI startup, upping the ante against Nvidia
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: AMD is acquiring World Labs, an AI startup, signaling increased competition against Nvidia.
The acquisition is a substantial financial move, valued at $8.2 billion.
The deal is anticipated to finalize before the end of the current year.

stories.title: Here's what actually happened in OpenAI's Australian gov't server hack
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: A security incident occurred involving OpenAI's government servers in Australia.
The breach allowed an agent to access sensitive data, including system information and source code.
The incident highlighted vulnerabilities related to insufficient safeguards within the system.

stories.title: OpenAI says planned GPT-6.1 is too insecure to release
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: OpenAI has reportedly halted the release of a planned GPT-6.1 iteration due to significant security concerns.
The decision highlights ongoing, critical trade-offs between model performance and safety in advanced AI systems.
The security challenges noted are comparable to those observed in existing publicly available AI models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its capability in conversational or creative text output.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the active LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the core NLP/LLM ecosystem, specifically using the 'text-generation' pipeline.
The tags indicate relevance to major frameworks like transformers and model formats like safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing privacy and on-device capability.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase when benchmarked using Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: AI researchers put out videos saying superintelligence is ‘exactly as dangerous as it sounds’
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: AI researchers are expressing significant concern regarding the existential risk posed by superintelligence.
Several prominent figures, including former employees from OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Anthropic, are featured in the interviews.
One researcher cited suggests the probability of human extinction due to AI is close to 50%.

stories.title: Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning
stories.author: Anirudh Goyal
bullet_points: Introduces 'agentic meta-reasoning' to manage complex, long-running AI agent tasks.
Addresses the challenge of controlling execution flow in advanced AI agents by making control choices explicit.
Separates task-level computation (workers) from high-level decision-making (controller) during inference.

stories.title: Breaking the Uniformity Trap: Scaling Video Diffusion Model via SplitMoE
stories.author: Fan Tang
bullet_points: Proposes SplitMoE to adapt Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) for scaling video diffusion models.
Identifies a 'uniformity trap' in current visual MoEs, where independent token routing fails with spatiotemporally redundant video data.
Addresses the challenge of semantically long-tailed and redundant video data that conventional MoE routing struggles with.

stories.title: Imagine3D-LLM: Teaching MLLMs to Imagine 3D Scenes Before Answering
stories.author: Sunghwan Hong
bullet_points: Addresses the core challenge of MLLMs struggling to build coherent 3D understanding from multi-view images.
Proposes 'Imagine3D-LLM' to teach Multimodal LLMs to mentally construct 3D scenes before generating answers.
Contributes to the growing research area of injecting explicit 3D awareness into current MLLM architectures.

stories.title: From Routing Signals to Selective Review: Visual regrounding in MoE VLMs
stories.author: Nanyun Peng
bullet_points: Addresses a critical failure mode in Vision-Language Models (VLMs): target-absence grounding failure, where models answer questions about absent objects.
Introduces a novel framework that leverages internal routing decisions within Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) VLMs for detection.
Moves beyond traditional methods (response analysis, hidden states) to proactively detect when a target is missing before generation.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new decision models allow for fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Apple’s ‘HomePad’ will reportedly launch on October 13th
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly set to launch a new smart home hub on October 13th.
The launch event will also feature a new HomePod mini and an upgraded Apple TV.
All new devices are expected to showcase Siri AI, Apple's overhauled AI assistant.

stories.title: BMW’s revamped i3 boasts up to 468 miles of range
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: BMW is relaunching the i3 as a new all-electric four-door sedan.
The revamped i3 is being built on BMW's new Neue Klasse platform.
The updated model promises a significant range increase of up to 468 miles.

stories.title: Suspected ShinyHunters leader arrested in the Netherlands
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: A 24-year-old Amsterdam man was arrested by Dutch police in connection with the hacking group ShinyHunters.
ShinyHunters is known for high-profile cyberattacks, including those targeting Ticketmaster, Rockstar Games, and the FBI.
The arrest occurred shortly before the hacking group claimed responsibility for recent attacks.

stories.title: Protesters gather at OpenAI’s DevDay
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: Protests occurred at OpenAI's annual DevDay event.
The central theme of the protests was a demand for 'PEOPLE OVER PROFIT' from OpenAI leadership.
Over a dozen organizations joined to sponsor the rally outside the event.

stories.title: Most powerful obesity drug yet: People lost up to 25% of weight in trial
stories.author: Beth Mole
bullet_points: Retatrutide is a novel, highly effective obesity drug.
The drug functions as a triple-hormone agonist, mimicking GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon.
Clinical trials showed participants achieving weight loss of up to 25%.

stories.title: NASA has a Dragon dilemma, and there appear to be no good answers
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: NASA is facing a complex decision regarding its use of SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft.
The article suggests there are no easy or satisfactory solutions to the current dilemma.
The narrative raises questions about SpaceX's operational priorities and potential self-interest.

stories.title: This study looks at how and with whom connected cars share your data
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: Connected cars and companion apps expose users to numerous data trackers.
The study investigates the mechanisms and parties involved in data sharing within the automotive ecosystem.
Highlights the growing privacy concerns associated with modern vehicle technology.

stories.title: Skill-Space Shooting for Autonomous Robot Policy Improvement
stories.author: Yang Gao
bullet_points: The research addresses the need for autonomous robots to improve their policies in the real world without constant human intervention.
It proposes a method, 'Skill-Space Shooting,' to enable scalable learning from experience.
The work aims to overcome limitations in current agentic systems that rely on foundation models but struggle with self-teaching.

stories.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ying Wei
bullet_points: STEPQuant addresses memory bottlenecks in LLMs by using fixed-size recurrent states instead of large KV caches.
Directly quantizing these recurrent states causes significant accuracy degradation due to error propagation.
The study identifies that quantization error impact is dependent on temporal factors, specifically how long the memory state persists.

stories.title: LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ion Stoica
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inference bottleneck in LLMs that use linear attention by compressing context into a fixed-size recurrent state.
It proposes 'LeapQuant' to improve efficiency by applying accurate recurrent state quantization.
The research tackles the trade-off between reducing computational cost via quantization and maintaining high model quality.

stories.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
stories.author: Gang Hua
bullet_points: The research addresses a key challenge in long-video understanding: maintaining the physical identity of entities across extended temporal spans.
Existing methods struggle because chronological descriptions and text entities fail to resolve when different objects share descriptions or when the same object is observed in disconnected events.
The proposed solution introduces 'Grounded Entity Biographies' to connect events belonging to the same specific entity, improving question-answering over long videos.

stories.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
stories.author: Heng Ji
bullet_points: The research explores 'test-time AI-for-AI,' focusing on how one AI (Builder) can improve the environment for another (Target) without retraining either model.
A novel concept, 'Meta-Skill,' is introduced to formalize reusable principles dictating when and what kind of support the Builder should provide.
The Builder learns these environmental construction principles by analyzing the execution feedback provided by the Target model on a development set.

stories.title: AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation
stories.author: Sercan Ö. Arık
bullet_points: Introduces AdviSD, a method where a small trainable advisor guides a frozen, large language model (LLM) executor using natural language.
The advisor learns not only from task rewards but also from feedback on completed interactions to refine its advice.
The research highlights a theoretical finding that plausible corrections, even if not changing execution, can negatively impact the advisor's learning in shared-parameter models.

stories.title: How Local Mixing Encodes Relative Position in Global NoPE Attention
stories.author: Beren Millidge
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inherent position invariance of standard attention mechanisms.
It proposes using local mixing layers to implicitly encode relative positional information, bypassing explicit positional encodings (NoPE).
This offers an alternative to established methods like Rotary Position Encoding (RoPE) in transformer models.

stories.title: Skill-Space Shooting for Autonomous Robot Policy Improvement
stories.author: Yang Gao
bullet_points: The research addresses the need for autonomous robots to improve their policies in the real world without constant human intervention.
It explores using agentic systems and foundation models to autonomously compose learned behaviors for task completion.
The paper introduces 'Skill-Space Shooting' as a method to facilitate this self-improvement, moving beyond initial training limitations.

stories.title: Breakdown of Local Denoising as Semantic Speciation
stories.author: Xun Gao
bullet_points: The research investigates two distinct temporal dynamics in generative models: a 'speciation window' (semantic commitment) and a 'nonlocality window' (context insufficiency).
The study posits a 'common cause' hypothesis linking these two windows, suggesting a deep relationship in model behavior.
The analysis uses the spatial distribution of semantic information to prove the necessary relationship between the nonlocality and speciation windows.

stories.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ying Wei
bullet_points: STEPQuant addresses memory bottlenecks in large language models by replacing large KV caches with fixed-size recurrent states.
Directly quantizing these recurrent states causes significant accuracy degradation due to error propagation across state updates.
The study identifies that the impact of quantization errors is dependent on both temporal persistence and spatial location within the state.

stories.title: LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ion Stoica
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inference bottleneck in modern LLMs that use linear attention mechanisms (like GDN and KDA).
It proposes 'LeapQuant,' a method to efficiently quantize the fixed-size recurrent state used in these models.
The research aims to reduce computational cost while mitigating the typical quality degradation associated with state quantization.

stories.title: A Spectral Theory of Distortion in LLM Graph Reconstruction: Sharp Bounds and Empirical Characterization
stories.author: Jianru Shen
bullet_points: The paper introduces a spectral theory to analyze distortion when Language Models (LLMs) reconstruct graphs.
It establishes sharp bounds for the Wasserstein distance between Laplacian spectra using edge counts.
The analysis provides a more nuanced characterization of LLM graph reconstruction quality beyond single aggregate distances.

stories.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
stories.author: Gang Hua
bullet_points: The research addresses a key limitation in long-video understanding: maintaining the physical identity of entities across extended temporal spans.
The proposed method, 'Grounded Entity Biographies,' aims to resolve ambiguity where different objects might share descriptions or the same object is observed in disconnected events.
This work is relevant to advanced video AI tasks, such as complex question answering over long-form video content.

stories.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
stories.author: Heng Ji
bullet_points: The research explores 'test-time AI-for-AI,' focusing on how one AI (Builder) can optimize the environment for another (Target) without retraining.
A novel concept, 'Meta-Skill,' is introduced to define reusable principles for when and what kind of environmental support the Builder should provide.
The Builder learns these meta-skills by analyzing the execution feedback provided by the Target model on a development set.

stories.title: AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation
stories.author: Sercan Ö. Arık
bullet_points: Introduces AdviSD, a method to guide large, frozen Language Models (LLMs) using a small, trainable advisor.
The advisor learns not only from task rewards but also from feedback gathered during completed interactions.
The research explores the complex impact of 'plausible corrections' on the advisor's learning, showing potential limitations in shared-parameter models.

stories.title: Multi-Agent Flow Matching with Decoupled Generative Guidance
stories.author: Fabio Pasqualetti
bullet_points: Addresses the lack of formal guarantees in generative modeling when satisfying hard constraints.
Focuses on the complexity of enforcing multi-agent constraints where requirements depend on multiple agents.
Proposes 'Multi-Agent Flow Matching with Decoupled Generative Guidance' to manage agent-specific guidance inputs independently.

stories.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ying Wei
bullet_points: STEPQuant addresses memory bottlenecks in large language models by replacing growing KV caches with fixed-size recurrent states.
Directly quantizing these recurrent states causes significant accuracy degradation due to error propagation across updates.
The study identifies that quantization error impact is dependent on temporal factors, specifically how long the memory state persists.

stories.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
stories.author: Gang Hua
bullet_points: Addresses a key challenge in long-video understanding: maintaining physical identity of entities across extended temporal spans.
Proposes a method, 'Grounded Entity Biographies,' to resolve ambiguity where multiple objects share descriptions or single objects are disconnected.
Focuses on improving question-answering systems for long-form video content by linking events to specific entities.

stories.title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision
stories.author: Mor Geva
bullet_points: Addresses a fundamental limitation in standard Transformer LMs: the unidirectional, feed-forward nature of information flow.
Introduces LIFT (Latent Information Feedback Transformer) to remove the bottleneck by allowing feedback between layers during pretraining.
Aims to improve model efficiency and capability by preventing the discarding of alternative continuations and reducing recomputation.

stories.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
stories.author: Heng Ji
bullet_points: The research explores 'test-time AI-for-AI,' where one AI (Builder) designs better execution environments for another (Target) without retraining.
A novel concept, 'Meta-Skill,' is introduced to define reusable principles for when and what kind of support the Builder should provide.
The Builder learns these meta-principles by analyzing the Target's execution feedback gathered during the development phase.

stories.title: AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation
stories.author: Sercan Ö. Arık
bullet_points: Introduces AdviSD, a method allowing a small advisor model to steer large, frozen LLMs using natural language advice.
The advisor learns not only from task rewards but also from feedback gathered during completed interactions.
The research explores the nuanced impact of plausible, non-executing corrections on the advisor's future decision-making, particularly in shared-parameter models.

stories.title: LongHarness Bench: Stress-Testing Language Model Harnesses for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Xi Ye
bullet_points: Introduces 'LongHarness Bench,' a new benchmark to rigorously test language model harnesses designed for long-context reasoning.
Addresses a gap in current evaluations where existing tests fail to differentiate between various long-context harness implementations.
The benchmark evaluates both the effectiveness (using diverse retrieval strategies) and the efficiency of these advanced LM harnesses.

stories.title: How Local Mixing Encodes Relative Position in Global NoPE Attention
stories.author: Beren Millidge
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inherent position invariance of standard attention mechanisms.
It proposes using local mixing layers to implicitly encode relative positional information, challenging the necessity of explicit positional encodings (NoPE).
This work relates to recent trends in efficient attention mechanisms like Sliding Window Attention (SWA) and Gated Linear Attention.

stories.title: Who's Accountable When the AI Was Just Following Instructions?
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: The article addresses the accountability gap when AI systems cause data leaks.
A specific incident involved an AI agent leaking internal company data for three weeks.
The core theme explores responsibility when AI acts based solely on programmed instructions.

stories.title: AI Agent Governance on AWS: Block Agents, Prove EU AI Act Compliance
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: Demonstrates practical application of AI agent governance using AWS Bedrock.
Highlights capabilities for proactive agent control (e.g., hard-blocking runaway agents) and data privacy (PII redaction).
Addresses emerging regulatory needs by showing how to export audit evidence for compliance with the EU AI Act.

stories.title: 14 Personal AI Agents in 2026: A Technical Guide to Architecture, Memory, Tools & Autonomy
stories.author: amananandrai
bullet_points: The article explores 14 distinct architectures for personal AI agents expected in 2026.
It provides a technical guide covering critical components like memory, tools integration, and autonomy.
It signals a shift towards a new era defined by sophisticated, personalized AI agents.
